name: Pie chart
purpose: Composition / proportion as a full ring, no centre figure — ported from Chart-donut.reference.html (wave-2 lane ③, 2026-08-05) with the inner radius dropped to 0 and the DV-D13 centre-total wiring removed (donut-only, per brief). Segment popover · table-view popover · legend-as-filter/isolate/highlight · value ⇄ % segmented toggle (baked variant groups) · optional title + H-stack head · high-contrast remap — all copied from the donut's Layer-2 verbatim.
when: answers=composition AND parts ≤ 5 AND total=not printed — yields to chart-donut (80, "composition, a centre total is meaningful") whenever a centre total is wanted, which is the only thing separating the two; yields to chart-stacked-area (64) when the split moves over time.

not-with.when: the same composition is already drawn as a ring with a centre total — pick one, pie or donut, not both

props.name: labelling
props.$note: spider = letter on a short leader outside the ring + vertical legend [swatch][letter][name]; direct = name + value in place, no legend. D-Q2 (spider vs direct default) stays OPEN — cited, not re-decided; both variants shown, same posture as the donut.

props.name: slices
props.$note: Maximum 6 (dv-pie-009); more → combine smallest into 'Other'. Values must sum to the total carried on data-total (dv-pie-010) even though no centre figure displays it.

props.name: empty
props.$note: No-data state = the Empty-state pattern by reference.

props.name: valueMode
props.$note: Segmented-control atom (.seg.sm) drives BAKED variant groups (data-dv-view) — direct labels AND the table column mirror the active mode. JS-off = value view.

props.name: title
props.$note: Optional visible title (.dv-title, t-cm-section-label) in the H-stack head; sr-only figcaption still names the chart when absent.

variants.name: spider + legend
variants.use: Default composition view; letters bridge chart ↔ legend (§04.3).

variants.name: direct labels
variants.use: Self-contained view (print/export-friendly); name + £value · % on each leader.

variants.name: no data
variants.use: Empty-state pattern in the chart frame.

tokens.font-family: type composites via markup class — DV-D08 ladder: letters/keys .t-cm-chart-key (12/700) · labels + legend + controls .t-cm-chart-label (12/500) · direct values .t-cm-chart-value (12/500 tabular) · table .t-cm-legal
tokens.series: data/series/1–5 (same series as the donut; identical measured contrast)
tokens.separation: stroke = background/default (page) at 2px on every segment (dv-004)
tokens.labels: text/default (ink) — spider letters and direct labels never sit ON the fills
tokens.$survey: No new tokens minted. ds-020 check: pie/donut carry NO axis or gridline CSS at all, so there is nothing to inherit or receipt under that fence for this pair.

motion.entry: RADIAL SWEEP RETURNS (ADR-0015: data-driven geometry is JS territory) — segments bake the sweep contract (data-cx/-cy/-ro/-a1/-a2, NO data-ri) + data-seq on annotations; the sweep hook itself is a dv-behaviour source edit = CONDUCTOR'S SERIAL. Baked state = full wedges + visible annotations, so JS-off / reduced-motion / pre-hook all render complete.
motion.hover: brightness(1.12/1.22) emphasis + dvTip popover (data-tip; replaces native <title>) + legend/segment highlight dims the OTHER groups.
motion.reducedMotion: Global collapse present (only hover transitions exist).

responsive.rule: Same DV-D02 exclusion as the donut — fixed geometry (compressing a circle distorts); .dv-stage scrolls if the container is narrower.

mustNotNeighbour: A second composition chart of the same data (pick one — pie or donut, not both)
Charts re-using these series colours for different data (dv-014)

accessibility.role: figure role="group" + aria-labelledby → sr-only figcaption; svg role="group", aria-label carries subject + total.
accessibility.name: Figcaption names the chart; every segment carries aria-label == data-tip == table (name, value, percentage — one source); the real table is the full data surface.
accessibility.keyboard: Segments = focus stops (tabindex 0 → dvTip on focus); legend rows = buttons (Enter toggles, Shift+Enter isolates); seg view switch + CSV + table dropdown all native buttons; table panel takes focus on open, Esc returns it.
accessibility.focus: 2px ink outline on segments/buttons/panel (focus-visible); seg buttons inset −2.
accessibility.nonText: Segment fills ≥3:1 vs the page both modes; identity = letter/name + position + table, never colour alone (1.4.1); 2px page strokes keep adjacent segments separable.

antiPatterns: Segment values that don't sum to the declared total (dv-pie-010)
Gapless segments without the 2px page stroke (dv-004)
White letters on segment fills (type26-013 — white type is red-only; label in ink outside the ring)
A pie without its real data table (dv-005)
Proportionally scaling the ring down (DV-D02 exclusion — it distorts)
Signalling a control's off state by dimming alone (the legend off-state is the hollow-swatch + data/axis grey recipe)
Recomputing arc geometry at runtime outside the sweep hook (geometry is generation-time; behaviour only toggles baked variants)
Porting the donut's centre-total / DV-D13 selection-follow wiring across (donut-only, explicitly fenced by the brief)

behaviour.fallback: With CSS on and JS off the spider/legend canvas renders as an EMPTY <svg> and no pie is drawn — dvRender is what fills it. The data is not lost and is not unlabelled: the figure carries a real <table class="dv-table"> inside a native <details>/<summary> disclosure (s116-D2), authored in the markup and not generated, so the five categories, their pounds and their percentage shares open and read with no script at all (dv-005 tabular alternative + the a11y spine). The engine REWRITES those same rows from the spec when it runs, so the popover value and the table value are one number by construction. The DIRECT-LABEL canvas stays baked, so a complete pie, its leaders and its in-place labels all render with JS off. Lost with JS off: the value popover, the DV-D11 legend filter/isolate, the value ⇄ percent toggle and Copy CSV.
behaviour.$note: Typed #260 (s259-D1 fast follower, pie lane). `script` addresses the ENGINE CORE — dv-render.js is where this component's behaviour begins; the wedges are drawn through its type registry by dv-render-donut.js, which is named in `partial`. THERE IS NO dv-render-pie: dv-render-donut registers BOTH `donut` and `pie` off one ring(ctx, hole) routine (a pie is that ring with ri = 0), so Chart-pie COMPOSES the donut partial rather than duplicating the trigonometry — the same reading _validate_dataviz.py's ENGINE_TEST_PAGE already commits to ("pie is the ri=0 arm of the same partial", mapping this snippet's driven receipt to _tests/chart-engine/donut.html). `partial` lists ALL FOUR registered AUTO-BEHAVIOUR names the snippet carries, per the schema's own wording and the chart-donut precedent.

slices.use: The parts of the whole drawn as full-ring segments.
slices.$status: ruled s140-D2 (Dave, 2026-08-09, via SLOTS-DRAFT-REVIEW s140-v1 export)

obeys.$why: Start at 12 o'clock, largest to smallest unless the categories have an inherent order - the angle contract for the sweep this meta's motion.entry bakes (data-cx/-cy/-ro/-a1/-a2, no data-ri), which is where the start angle and the segment order are fixed, at generation time.

Label plus exact proportional value per slice, with indicator lines when segments crowd, is precisely this meta's `labelling` = spider default: the leader line IS the indicator line the rule asks for.
Direct labelling adjacent to segments is the meta's second declared variant ('direct labels'), so the rule names one of the two things this component can be.
Labels inside a slice only where they stay readable is the TASTE half of the labelling choice, and it is why this meta's antiPatterns ban white type on the fills and put labels outside the ring.

Slice-ordering direction has to be checked against assistive technology, and this meta makes every segment a focus stop with aria-label == data-tip == table - the order those stops are read in is what the rule is about.

Never enlarge or pull out a slice to emphasise it: the meta has no exploded variant and its motion block moves segments only by a radial sweep that ends flush, so the rule is the reason no such variant exists.
Proportion of a set total ONLY, never group-to-group comparison - this is the `when` gate of the meta stated from the guidance side, and it is what sends comparison to chart-bar.

Maximum 6 slices, pie and doughnut alike: the meta's `slices` prop cites this rule by id and carries the 'combine the smallest into Other' remedy, so the edge records a binding the meta already states in prose.

Values must add up to the declared total: this meta prints NO centre figure, so data-total is the only place the total lives and the arithmetic is unverifiable by eye - the rule binds harder here than on the donut, not less.
Always indicate rounding: the value ⇄ percent toggle in this meta's `valueMode` prop is exactly where rounded percentages appear, and the rule is the contract that toggle has to honour.

Never omit data to distort the reading: with the engine off this meta still hands over the whole set - the five categories, their pounds and their percentage shares open and read with no script at all - because the table is authored in the markup, not generated.

Minimum 2px separation between colour blocks, never colour alone to separate values: this meta's `tokens.separation` cites the rule by id as a page-coloured 2px stroke on every segment, and its antiPatterns ban the gapless case.

A tabular alternative, always: the meta's antiPatterns cite this rule by id - "A pie without its real data table (dv-005)" - and the behaviour block names the real dv-table inside a native details/summary as the thing that survives JS-off.

The circular-chart limb of this rule - direct labelling adjacent to segments - is this meta's `labelling` enum itself: direct is name + value in place, no legend, which is why the prop has two values and not one.

All the data visible at the smallest viewport, else explicit navigation: this meta cannot answer by compressing, because compressing a circle distorts, so its declared answer at narrow widths is the .dv-stage scroll - the rule's else-branch, chosen deliberately.

Horizontal scroll only as a last resort, and here it IS the last resort: the ring has fixed geometry and cannot compress, so ".dv-stage scrolls if the container is narrower" is the fallback this rule fences rather than a layout choice - the clause that settled this cell for chart-pie.

Flat two-dimensional fills only, no 3D and no gradient: every fill this meta declares is one token - data/series/1–5, the same series as the donut - carried on baked wedges with a page-coloured stroke, so there is no gradient, bevel or shadow layer anywhere in the component.

Nothing that obscures the data: the one thing this meta floats over the ring is the dvTip popover, and its emphasis mechanism is subtractive - legend/segment highlight dims the OTHER groups - so nothing is drawn on top to make a slice stand out.
Colour may not carry the narrative alone, and this meta says so in its own words: identity = letter/name + position + table, never colour alone.
Colour focuses attention and is never the chart's background: this meta's `tokens.surface` is background/default, the page's own ground, and the only colour it spends is on the wedges themselves.

Same data, same colour across the journey: this meta's `mustNotNeighbour` cites the rule by id - charts re-using these series colours for different data - which is the journey-scope half of the rule stated as a neighbour ban.

Chart building blocks must clear 3:1: this meta states the floor for its fills (segment fills ≥3:1 vs the page both modes), and its `$survey` records why the rule's axis/gridline limb has nothing to bind to here - pie/donut carry NO axis or gridline CSS at all.

Only palette colours in charts: every colour this meta names is a token role - series, separation, leaders, labels, surface - and the `$survey` records "No new tokens minted", so there is no path by which a raw hex reaches a wedge.

Different colours within a single-variable circular chart: the `slices` slot accepts one capability, proportion-slices, and the series token spends a different colour on each part of that one variable.

Adjacent saturated near-complementary fills shimmer, and the rule names the dv-004 gap as its structural defence: on a ring EVERY pair is adjacent, and this meta already carries that defence as a 2px page stroke on every segment, with the gapless case banned in antiPatterns.

mustNotNeighbour.$note: A second composition chart of the same data (pick one — pie or donut, not both)
Charts re-using these series colours for different data (dv-014)
